function.mechanism: Hydroxypropyl substitution of starch modifies physicochemical behavior and supports thickening, stabilization, and emulsification functions in food systems.
common_food_categories: processed foods using food starch-modified ingredients

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation of modified starches including E1440 concluded no need for a numerical ADI; historical SCF/JECFA ADI framing was not specified.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern for modified starches (including E1440) at reported uses and use levels for the general population.

fda.notes: Hydroxypropyl starch is handled under the food starch-modified food additive framework; no explicit hydroxypropyl starch listing was found in searched Part 182/184 GRAS XML endpoints.

adi.basis: JECFA hydroxypropyl starch page lists ADI NOT SPECIFIED in toxicological entries; 2018 entry is specification-only.

concerns.summary: EFSA indicates modified starches are hydrolyzed and then fermented by intestinal microbiota, implying GI physiological interaction but not a demonstrated safety signal at approved uses.
Rat studies on related hydroxypropyl-modified starches reported altered fecal bile acid excretion and lower Zn/Fe absorption under specific test conditions.
A chronic mouse feeding study with hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate reported adaptive GI/renal findings at high dietary inclusion but no evidence of carcinogenicity for tested products.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 concluded no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for modified starches including E1440 and no need for a numerical ADI.
JECFA hydroxypropyl starch entries report ADI NOT SPECIFIED.
No direct IARC classification entry found for hydroxypropyl starch (E1440/CAS 9049-76-7) in the searched dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI exceedance cannot be computed because EFSA/JECFA use non-numerical ADI framing for this context. EFSA accessible abstract reports group-level modified starch exposure figures rather than E1440-only intake.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current regulatory evidence is permissive (EFSA/JECFA non-numerical ADI framing and no-safety-concern conclusion; US approval under 21 CFR 172.892 with reagent/residual limits). Countervailing factors are limited additive-specific modern long-term human safety data and some high-dose findings in related modified-starch animal studies.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation including E1440: no safety concern and no numerical ADI
JECFA hydroxypropyl starch ADI entries: NOT SPECIFIED
US regulatory coverage in 21 CFR 172.892 with explicit process/reagent limits
No direct IARC classification found for E1440
